html:
SMTO-GWT-0030 — A computer couldn't accept a file copy instruction

GUID: ea8cf5eb-7502-4eb7-ba7f-129daac41e72
Slug: gateway-transfer-invalid
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gwt

What happened

  • While copying a file between two computers, SMTO sent a copy instruction that the receiving Gateway could not accept, so that step was not carried out. Earlier steps of the same copy may already have happened.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, expand each computer involved in the copy, and under Software updates select Check for updates. Install any update offered. A Gateway on a different version from SMTO can disagree about what a copy instruction must contain.
  2. On the receiving computer, look in the destination folder for a partial or finished copy of the file. Earlier steps of the same copy may already have created part of the file.
  3. Ask SMTO to copy the file again in a new message. Once both sides agree on the instruction format, a new copy can be accepted.

What success looks like

  • The copy finishes and the Task reports the file at its destination.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, including which two computers were involved. Don't keep repeating the same copy before updating; it will be refused the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gateway rejected a file-transfer request because its encoding, extra fields or missing required fields failed the transfer protocol validation, before the transfer service ran that action.

What this means

  • Transfer request parsing or action-specific validation rejected the payload's encoding, extra fields or missing required fields before the transfer service call. This applies to inbound and outbound routes. Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Transfer request parsing or action-specific validation rejected the payload's encoding, extra fields or missing required fields before the transfer service call. This applies to inbound and outbound routes.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the rejected action with its allowed and required fields and the negotiated binary or JSON wire format.

How to fix it

  • TransferRequest validation (strict, extra='forbid') or its action_fields validator in src/gateway_core/transfer_contract.py rejected the request on the inbound or outbound route. Compare the Server and Gateway versions, since protocol skew is the usual cause; update the Gateway to the Server's release, then inspect the destination state before starting a new transfer with a new transfer ID.
  • Correct the transfer action's fields using the current supported protocol; preserve transfer identity and scope.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The corrected transfer action validates under the same transfer identity and intended source and destination.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
